methods.name: MacKinnon (1994) response-surface p-values of the Dickey-Fuller t (no constant, constant, constant and trend), as plm:::padf(p.approx = 'MacKinnon1994')
methods.reference: plm:::padf(q, exo = 'none' | 'intercept' | 'trend', p.approx = 'MacKinnon1994'); urca::punitroot(q, N = Inf, trend) for the deviation
quantities: p on a 191-point grid (-6.5 to 3) for each model, inside the range where the response surface is monotone

deviations.quantity: p_nc, p_c, p_ct (plm's default p.approx = MacKinnon1996)
deviations.note: p2a evaluates MacKinnon's (1994) response surface, plm's p.approx without urca, and not MacKinnon's (1996) tabulated distribution that urca::punitroot interpolates (plm's default with urca installed). On the grid the two differ by at most 0.004 in p inside the monotone range (1% relative for p between 0.01 and 0.99, more in the far tails)

deviations.quantity: p94_intercept above t = 2.74, p94_trend above t = 0.70 (the cubic's local maximum) and every model below the quadratic's vertex (t = -19.05, -18.83, -16.18)
deviations.note: plm evaluates the polynomials outside the range where they rise, so its p falls again (0.25 at t = 3 with a trend); p2a holds p at its value at the turning point, MacKinnon's (1994) tau_min and tau_max, so p is non-decreasing in t. These grid points are asserted constant and non-decreasing in the same test

quantities: IPS W-tbar, p and the averaged table moments: intercept, trend; lags 1 and 3 (T = 50), 1, 2 and 4 (T = 15)

methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 500 (120 for the short case): statistics 1e-6 relative, p-values 1e-6 relative (abs 1e-12); table moments 1e-14
